home.whyTitle: Preserving evidence for a difficult-to-study species
home.whyText: The Bornean bay cat combines a restricted distribution, forest association and a still-limited knowledge base. This project brings public data together so each record can be reviewed in context.

home.limitsTitle: Available data do not tell the whole story
home.limitsText: An occurrence is not abundance and a public sequence is not population-level genetic diversity. A missing record does not demonstrate species absence.

taxonomy.title: Taxonomy
taxonomy.description: Name relationships backed by public records, without building a private taxonomy.
taxonomy.name: Name
taxonomy.relationshipText: Catopuma badia is the accepted name. Pardofelis badia is a historical or alternative name that can still appear in catalogues, papers and genetic records.
taxonomy.searchText: Catopuma temminckii belongs to the same genus, Catopuma. That genus-level relationship helps guide searches but is not presented here as a new phylogenetic inference.
taxonomy.searchHistory: Historical names matter: searching both names reduces the risk of missing literature or molecular records archived under an earlier taxonomic combination.

research.metadataNote: Description based on bibliographic metadata; it does not reproduce an abstract or full text.

profile.title: Species Profile
profile.description: A traceable synthesis of what is available and what remains unknown.
profile.commonNameValue: Bornean bay cat / Borneo bay cat
profile.biologyText: The species is a forest-associated felid endemic to Borneo. Available public information describes a secretive species that is difficult to detect, so direct observation is limited.
profile.habitatText: Its association with forest makes habitat quality, continuity and protection central to conservation planning.
profile.conservationText: Its restricted distribution in Borneo and forest dependence make it important to document where it occurs and what evidence exists about its threats.
profile.threatsText: Forest loss and fragmentation, together with hunting, trapping and illegal capture, are documented or identified as relevant conservation risks; their local magnitude may be uncertain.
profile.knownDistribution: Known distribution is restricted to Borneo; GBIF records document published observations or specimens, not abundance.
profile.knownTaxonomy: Catopuma badia is the accepted name; Pardofelis badia appears as a historical or alternative name in databases.
profile.knownRecords: NCBI/GenBank provides public sequence records and PubMed provides searchable literature metadata.
profile.unknownPopulation: Population size, trend and connectivity are not estimated by this project.
profile.unknownGenetics: Available sequence records do not establish population-level genetic diversity.
profile.unknownDistribution: True distribution, detectability and occupancy beyond public records remain uncertain.
profile.sourcesText: Conservation claims link to Cat Specialist Group/IUCN resources for context. This profile is not an official IUCN assessment.

availability.title: Data Availability
availability.description: Per-source status retrieved on demand; a provider failure is not turned into a zero.
availability.gbifLimit: Maximum window of 100 occurrences per query; does not represent abundance.
availability.ncbiLimit: Public sequence records returned by search; not population diversity.
availability.boldLimit: Adapter is not connected because endpoint/CORS access is not verified.
availability.crossrefLimit: Documented reference; not queried by the application.
availability.dryadLimit: Documented reference; not queried by the application.
availability.unavailableLimit: The query failed; no invented count is shown.

conservation.iucn: IUCN Red List / Cat Specialist Group
conservation.note: This site is not an official IUCN assessment. It summarizes context and links sources for consultation.
conservation.statusText: The species is classified as Endangered in the IUCN/Cat Specialist Group context; consult the official source for assessment scope and date.
conservation.habitatText: Forest conversion and fragmentation can reduce available habitat and connectivity. Magnitude varies among landscapes and is not estimated here.
conservation.captureText: Hunting, trapping and illegal capture are documented or identified as relevant threats for small felids; public data do not quantify local incidence.
conservation.forestText: The species' association with forest environments makes conserving continuous forest and managing edges plausible priorities, not a measured occupancy result.
conservation.protectedText: Protected areas may contribute to habitat conservation, but their presence alone does not demonstrate effective protection of the species.
conservation.gapsText: Uncertainty remains around distribution, detectability, abundance, connectivity and population genetics.
conservation.geneticsText: Genetic data can help investigate taxonomic identity, provenance and connectivity when sampling and study design support those questions. Public sequence records alone do not estimate population diversity.
conservation.prioritiesText: Improve repeatable monitoring, conserve and connect forests, document threats and make uncertainty explicit for every inference.
conservation.projectTitle: What this project can realistically contribute
conservation.projectText: It integrates public occurrence records, sequences and literature with visible provenance. It can improve discovery and reproducibility; it cannot replace fieldwork, an IUCN assessment or population analyses.
conservation.disclaimer: Notice: this page is not an official IUCN assessment.

methodology.directText: Responses from public APIs, retaining source, sourceId, scientificName, dataset and original URL.
methodology.derivedText: Counts, filters and unique genes/markers are calculated over queried records. Population genetic parameters are not estimated.
methodology.limitsText: Coverage depends on each provider, its rate limits, taxonomy and availability. Missing records do not prove species absence.
methodology.refreshText: Queries run on demand and are cached locally for the session; each record retains its retrieval time.
methodology.unknownText: A missing field is shown as Not available. Coordinates, markers, publications and genetic values are never filled by inference.
methodology.retrievalText: GBIF, NCBI/GenBank and PubMed are queried through the existing adapters. Responses are normalized to local types and retain provenance links.
methodology.coordinatesText: Only numeric coordinates present in the normalized response are mapped; the map does not turn text localities into points.
methodology.taxonomyText: Catopuma badia and the historical name Pardofelis badia are queried where the source permits. Normalization does not prove new synonymy.
methodology.provenanceText: Observed means returned by the source. Derived means counts or filters calculated locally. Unknown remains explicit.
methodology.inferenceText: Public sequence availability is not equivalent to population-level genetic diversity. The project does not estimate structure, gene flow, effective size or allele frequencies.
